messages:
customer_acct: Hi team — after we migrated traffic to the new VPC endpoint (vpce-0abc1234) API calls from our office intermittently fail with 403s. Happens only from corp network, works from home/mobile. No config changes on our side besides point DNS to privatelink.

sanjay_support: Thanks, sorry you're hitting this. Quick Qs: which region, and can you paste a failing curl -v output? Also, are you going through a corporate HTTP/S proxy or any TLS inspection appliance?

customer_acct: us-east-1. Yes we have an outbound proxy (blueproxy) that does TLS inspection. Here's a short curl I ran from a laptop on corp net: 

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/v1/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.internal/v1/predict
*   Trying 10.11.22.33...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.internal (10.11.22.33) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.2 connection established
* ALPN, server accepted to use http/1.1
* Server certificate: BlueCorp Proxy CA
* SSL: certificate subject name 'blueproxy.corp' does not match 'api.redwood.internal'
> POST /v1/predict HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.internal\n> ...\n< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n< content-type: application/json\n< {"error":"auth.failed","message":"invalid client cert or host"}
```

customer_acct: We see BlueCorp cert in the chain and immediate 403. From home the cert is our normal Redwood cert and requests work fine.

emma_netops: That pattern screams TLS interception by the corp proxy. PrivateLink + Private DNS means your clients resolve api.redwood.internal to the VPCE IP, but if a middlebox is doing TLS MITM and re-signing certs, the server (or our edge) might reject the connection if SNI/host mismatch or client mTLS expectations fail.

jess_prodeng: Adding: our frontdoor uses SNI-based routing to select customer tenant/route. If the proxy rewrites SNI or presents its own cert, the TLS handshake completes but the application layer sees wrong host metadata and will reject/route incorrectly -> 403.

customer_acct: Is there a way to confirm the proxy is rewriting SNI vs just replacing cert? I can run tcpdump but want precise repro steps to show to infra team.

sanjay_support: Two quick checks: 1) curl with --resolve to bypass DNS and hit the VPCE IP directly, and 2) openssl s_client -connect <vpce-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.internal to inspect SNI and cert chain. If the cert CN/issuer is BlueCorp Proxy CA then TLS inspection is active.

customer_acct: Ran both, pasted outputs: 

```
# 1) bypass DNS
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.11.22.33 https://api.redwood.internal/v1/predict
* Connected to 10.11.22.33 (10.11.22.33) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
* Server certificate: BlueCorp Proxy CA
* SSL: certificate subject name 'blueproxy.corp' does not match 'api.redwood.internal'
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"auth.failed"}

# 2) openssl
openssl s_client -connect 10.11.22.33:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -showcerts
subject=/CN=blueproxy.corp
issuer=/CN=BlueCorp Proxy CA
---
no intermediate from origin
```

customer_acct: So proxy is intercepting and resigning certs.

jess_prodeng: Confirmed. Root cause: TLS inspection / proxy doing MITM. Two failure modes with PrivateLink: 1) proxy replaces server cert so host verification fails (client side) or 2) proxy strips/replaces SNI so our gateway cannot route to the correct tenant -> 403/401. Looks like in your case the gateway sees proxy-supplied SNI/CN and rejects.

emma_netops: Repro steps for your infra team to validate and fix: 
1) From corp host: run `openssl s_client -connect <vpce-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -brief` and verify cert issuer.
2) tcpdump on the host or proxy to capture TLS ClientHello and check SNI field: `sudo tcpdump -w mitm.pcap -s 0 host <vpce-ip> and port 443` then open in wireshark and inspect Client Hello > Server Name .
3) If proxy is re-signing, either configure the proxy to bypass TLS inspection for `*.redwood.internal` (preferred) OR add an explicit egress allowlist for the VPCE IP and hostnames to go direct.

customer_acct: Our security team says they can't fully disable inspection, but they can add bypass rules per hostname. Anything specific they need to allow?

sanjay_support: They should allow TLS passthrough for api.redwood.internal and any subdomains in use, and ensure SNI is preserved. Also allow outbound to our VPCE IP range and don't rewrite Host or SNI.

jess_prodeng: As a short-term workaround, if your proxy supports CONNECT-level passthrough for specific hostnames, that will let the handshake reach our edge unmodified. Long-term: avoid terminating TLS for Redwood hostnames.

customer_acct: We added a bypass rule for api.redwood.internal -> immediate relief, errors dropped. Thanks. Any server-side mitigations on Redwood we can use if the customer can't change proxy?

sre_oncall: Server-side options are limited because proxy fundamentally breaks end-to-end TLS. We can add more explicit error logging to surface "SNI mismatch / proxy detected" in our logs to help you demonstrate to security, and we can support IP-based allowlisting if you provide static egress IPs, but the secure fix is to let TLS passthrough.

customer_acct: Can you share the logs we should show to our security team?

sanjay_support: We'll attach a short diagnostic snippet you can forward. Example lines we see when proxy is present: 
```
2026-03-16T15:12:03Z frontdoor-01 WARN tls: client presented cert CN=blueproxy.corp, expected sni=api.redwood.internal, rejecting connection
2026-03-16T15:12:03Z gateway-02 INFO auth: tenant_lookup failed for sni=blueproxy.corp, returned 403
```

jess_prodeng: Also include the openssl/curl outputs you captured and the pcap showing ClientHello SNI rewrites. Security teams usually accept the pcap + s_client evidence.

customer_acct: Great — forwarding now. Adding :thumbsup: to the infra ticket. We'll re-open if anything else pops up.

sanjay_support: Thanks — glad that fixed it. Reopen if you see any drift. We'll follow up to add clearer doc in our PrivateLink troubleshooting guide about TLS inspection and SNI. :white_check_mark:

deploy_bot: scheduled-run:privatelink-doc-update #367 will be created by docs-bot for support follow-up

jess_prodeng: Filing internal follow-up to propose a KB entry with reproduction steps and recommended proxy bypass rules.

customer_acct: Appreciate the help, team.
